column1: This manual is aligned with the current manuscript taxonomy: vulnerabilities are classified by ROS version and CIA; reliability faults are classified as CODE or SEM, with BDF, SEF, GPE, ICF, and BSE as the only reliability leaf codes.

column3: Use only the actual study object, implementation, or evaluation. Background, related work, and future work do not count.
column5: Code Both merely because ROS 2 is mentioned.

column3: Malicious exploitation, unauthorized behavior, or a missing security policy → VUL; non-malicious internal fault → REL.
column5: Automatically code BOTH because an attack causes a crash.

column3: For VUL, select C, I, or A. For REL, select CODE or SEM.

column3: Code the earliest, most specific, evidence-supported primary root-cause locus.
column5: Assign multiple reliability codes to the same fault instance based on its symptoms.

column3: A study may receive multiple codes, but each code must correspond to a distinct fault instance or fault family and have separate evidence.
column5: Add unevaluated codes merely because a tool claims broad support.
column6: Topic mismatch = ICF; unit mismatch = BSE.

column3: The defect code describes the root cause; Impact describes the system consequence. Keep them separate.
column5: Use crash, delay, or wrong motion as a defect code.

column5: Write only “the paper discusses this issue.”

column1: A node subscribes to the wrong topic name, so the robot does not move.
column3: BSE
column5: The primary root cause is interface wiring; immobility is only the consequence.
column6: Evidence of the incorrect topic/remap and the missing message flow.

column1: The message arrives correctly, but degrees are interpreted as radians.
column3: ICF
column5: The interface works; the defect lies in physical semantics.
column6: Expected unit, actual unit, and the resulting incorrect value or behavior.

column1: A long-running callback causes queue overflow and message loss.
column3: ICF
column5: The root cause is the execution/queue mechanism, not the interface contract.
column6: Callback duration, queue state, and timing traces.

column1: ROS 2 endpoints cannot communicate because their QoS settings are incompatible.
column3: SEF
column5: Compatibility or configuration prevents interaction.
column6: QoS profiles of both endpoints and incompatibility logs.

column1: A missing runtime dependency in package.xml causes deployment failure.
column3: GPE
column5: The root cause lies in dependency metadata.

column1: A shared variable lacks locking and causes a data race.
column3: SEF
column5: This is a generic synchronization defect; use SEF only when callback-group or executor configuration is the cause.
column6: Source code, locking behavior, and sanitizer or trace evidence.

column1: An attacker changes control gains through an unprotected parameter interface.
column3: BSE
column5: The primary mechanism is unauthorized modification; add BSE only if the paper separately analyzes a benign misconfiguration of the same parameter.
column6: Attack model, parameter write, and resulting behavioral change.

column1: An attack causes a node crash.
column3: Do not automatically add REL or BOTH
column5: The crash is an impact. Code BOTH only when an independent internal reliability fault is also analyzed.
column6: Exploit chain, vulnerability mechanism, and crash evidence.
